sections.text: Nano-composite brush plating technology is not only a new technology in surface engineering, but also a key technology for manufacturing precision ceramic materials. It is a new method. Nano-composite brush plating technology is a combination of nano technology and traditional brush plating technology, which not only maintains the functions of brush plating, electroplating, chemical plating and other technologies, but also expands their application scope and has gained wider and stronger applications.
(1) Improving the wear resistance of part surfaces

By adding nano-ceramic particles into the plating solution to carry out nano-composite brush plating, when nano-ceramic particle powder is dispersed in the base metal coating, it forms a full metal-ceramic composite coating. The brush plating coating contains a large number of nano-ceramic hard particles, making the brush plating layer highly wear-resistant. Using this kind of brush plating can replace the processes of chrome plating, carburizing, nitriding, and hard chromium plating, etc.
(2) Reducing the surface roughness of parts

By adding nano-scale particles with reduced friction (such as nano-diamond particles, molybdenum disulfide, graphite, etc.) into the brush plating solution for nano-composite brush plating, the obtained composite coating has a low friction coefficient. This type of nano-composite brush plating solution with dispersed nano particles distributed within it has the characteristic of several individual reduced areas reaching the effect of reducing friction of parts, and can also reduce the wear of parts and extend their service life.
(3) Improving the high-temperature wear resistance of part surfaces

By adding metal-ceramic powder brush plating coating material into the nano-composite brush plating, particularly the metal-ceramic coating which has excellent high-temperature resistance. When the brush plating layer is working at high temperatures, the ceramic phase can maintain high-temperature stability, and the brush plating layer as a whole can also serve as support, effectively improving the high-temperature wear resistance of the brush plating layer.
(4) Improving the fatigue resistance of part surfaces

Many surface engineering techniques require plating layers, which can also be used to restore damaged part dimensions and geometric shapes, improve part surface corrosion resistance, wear resistance, and can withstand alternating loads. Nano-composite brush plating layers have relatively high fatigue resistance.

This "limiting post" can effectively limit the crystal within the coating as a type of internal stress. The existence of this also changes the stress state of the crystal. Therefore, the nano-composite brush plating layer has excellent fatigue resistance, which is far superior to ordinary brush plating layers.
(5) Improving the service performance of metal surfaces

Many parts or workpieces are made from or use metallic coatings, mainly to achieve good electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, corrosion resistance, anti-fouling and other properties. The forming process is to create a colored metal intermediate layer (liquid plating, copper alloy brush plating treatment may turn green, brass color) (solid silver plating), which can all be applied using this technology.
(6) Practical aspects of re-manufacturing are mainly focused on brush

The focus of the re-manufacturing process is to first determine the original part dimensions and geometric tolerances. Therefore, the traditional brush plating method is used first for rapid restoration of the plating layer to the required dimensional tolerance on the part surface, and then nano-composite brush plating technology is used for dimensional correction on the surface brush plating layer as the working layer, to improve the part surface properties. Using brush plating or brush plating + brush plating nano-composite coating repair and supplementation on parts (such as scratches, pitting, cracks on journal, piston rod, etc.) is a fast and meaningful technology.
Because brush plating technology has become a traditional or common technology, it is relatively familiar. Here, this is not further elaborated.

Laser remanufacturing technology is mainly aimed at surface grinding, corrosion, impact, abrasion and other damaged parts (including dimensions and precision), and at the same time improving the wear resistance of re-processed parts. 3) Tool materials

Due to the metal cladding layer and thermal spray coating generally having relatively high hardness and heat resistance, especially high hardness and high cutting force generation during machining and large cutting forces, the accelerated tool wear is one of the major difficulties. Even using cemented carbide tools for cutting, the tool life is limited. This creates production efficiency issues.
4) Thermal spray coating is prone to delamination

The bond strength between the thermal spray coating and the substrate is not very high. Using the brush plating process, the coating connected with the body structure acts as a composite machine tool structure. The bond tensile strength is generally 30-50MPa. Due to the coating being relatively thin, it is difficult to perform cutting machining, with the risk of cutting through to a certain extent. The coating is easily peeled off and is prone to this.

The cladding layer has a certain hardness and wear resistance. When performing cutting machining, the vibration and impact forces generated during machining are not less than the service life of turning tools, and to ensure the tool has a certain service life. According to the current commonly used tool materials and cutting performance characteristics, roughing may use carbide grades such as YG8, YT5, YW1 and other tools. These tool materials have good toughness, moderate strength and better cutting performance. When adding cutting fluid for turning, the tool should also have good heat resistance. When cutting, attention should also be paid to the remaining cooling after cutting of the residual hardness of the surface, "holes", and vibration. At this time, the tool should have relatively good toughness and hardness, such as cemented carbide YT15 tools.
2. Turning of Stainless Steel Cladding Layers

Stainless steel cladding layers mostly use austenitic stainless steel welding rod for cladding, which is composed of austenite. Austenitic stainless steel has good ductility, work hardening tendency during processing and cutting, and with a cutting hardness of 45 HRC for 1/3, austenitic stainless steel also has difficult-to-machine characteristics.

For stainless steel cladding layers, YT cemented carbide tools cannot be used because the Ti in YT cemented carbide and the elements of the workpiece material such as iron cause affinity and surface adhesion, leading to chipping. Therefore, it is generally recommended to use YG, YH, or YW type cemented carbide tools, which can also achieve high-performance high-speed cutting tools. Tool geometric parameters: rake angle 5°~6°; relief angle 4°~6°; inclination angle -5°~0°; approach angle reduced as small as possible. Large nose radius, cutting depth a_p = 1.5~2mm, f = 0.3~0.4mm/r, v_c = 14~18m/min.
6.6.2.1 Turning of Cladding Layers

Using cladding methods to restore the original dimensions of worn parts is a very common remanufacturing method. The cladding layer has a certain hardness and wear resistance, and since the cladding method for rapid restoration uses cladding welding rod materials, the thickness variation is large and uneven, surface oxidation and internal structural changes. Whether the cladding layer or process integrity is complete requires careful consideration and attention.
1. Low alloy steel cladding layer turning

Low alloy cladding layers, due to the different carbon content of the cladding welding rod, the obtained cladding layer hardness is also different. From the surface hardness, it is medium to high hardness cladding layers and high hardness cladding layers. In the remanufacturing process, the commonly used medium hardness cladding layers, the cladding layer structure after cooling is mainly martensite. The cladding layer has a small amount of ferrite structure. After cooling to completion, it produces martensitic lath structure. Pay attention to the cooling rate. The hardness of medium hardness cladding layers is 200~350HBW (such as Type 107 welding rod, the cladding layer hardness is approximately 250HBW; Type 127 welding rod, the cladding layer hardness is approximately 350HBW). The cladding layer base metal contains Cr, Mn and other alloy elements dissolved into the ferrite body, which leads to solid solution strengthening and causes the cladding layer to have a certain degree of hardness and wear resistance, as well as good impact resistance.
6.6.2.2 Turning of Thermal Spray Coatings

The main characteristic of thermal spray coatings is high hardness with good wear resistance. Their hardness can reach 50~70HRC. Because this is a type of thermal spray coating, it can be very difficult to machine. For specific situations, it is still necessary to conduct turning operations. The tool parameters and various cutting parameters need to meet certain special requirements.
